purpose: Research item A8 — the intelligibility gate: separate -> RMS-VAD vocal-activity segmentation -> per-language ASR -> BOTH softened PER and case-insensitive WER. Every parameter below carries the exact source it was read from. music_studio/vocal_activity.py and music_studio/per_gate.py consume this file; neither holds a threshold of its own.
why_this_file_exists: A VAD threshold is exactly the class of value this project has paid for guessing once: a guessed motion floor of 0.08 rejected all seven correct shots where the calibrated value was 0.0007 (MANDATE CLAUSE 7). The local research corpus recorded S17's RESULTS (23.02 % -> 20.35 %) but not its PARAMETERS, so the primary was read this session.

S17_paper.citation: Jaza Syed, Ivan Meresman-Higgs, Ondřej Cífka, Mark Sandler. 'Exploiting Music Source Separation for Automatic Lyrics Transcription with Whisper'. IEEE ICMEW 2025 (In press). arXiv:2506.15514, published 2025-06-18.
S17_paper.read_as: [FULL] — fetched and read this session; the RMS-VAD method section, Cut & Merge parameters, Tables III/IV/V discussion and the deletions analysis were read directly.
S17_paper.verbatim_parameters: For "Cut & Merge", we use onset and offset thresholds of 0.1, a minimum silence duration of 1 s and a maximum segment length of 30 s, matching Whisper's input duration.
S17_paper.verbatim_algorithm: 1) Obtain separated vocals with a source separation model 2) Compute VAD[n] for the separated vocals 3) Obtain boundaries from VAD[n] using "Cut & Merge"
S17_paper.gap_in_the_paper: the frame size N is defined SYMBOLICALLY in equation (2) and its numeric value is never stated in the text. That gap is why the authors' code was read as well.

S17_code.read_as: [FULL] — fetched and read this session. The README names `get_speech_timestamps_rms` as the paper's VAD step, and the function's body supplies every value the paper left symbolic.
S17_code.licence_note: the repository's licence was NOT opened this session. Nothing is copied from it: the parameters are FACTS about a published method, and our implementation is our own code. Before any code-level reuse the licence must be read.

stage_1_separation.rule: the vocal signal is obtained by separation, and it is used for MEASUREMENT ONLY (MANDATE CLAUSE 15 forbids shipping a separated stem).
stage_1_separation.our_separator: SCNet XL IHF, 4-stem — music_studio/data/separators.json, chosen on SDR with an MIT licence, already run on the GPU instance
stage_1_separation.their_separator: Hybrid Demucs mdx (vocals SDR 7.97 dB) and mdx_extra (8.76 dB); long-form experiments used mdx_extra only
stage_1_separation.measured_caveat_that_changes_expectation: S17 line 129: 'RMS-VAD shows similar performance with original and separated audio, indicating that the improvement comes from better segment boundaries rather than improved vocal quality after separation.' So for Jam-ALT the gain is SEGMENTATION, not clarity. Our local claim C09 credits both; the primary credits boundaries. Recorded as a refinement of C09, not a contradiction of the outcome numbers.

rms_hop_samples.source: S17 code: window_size_samples=512, documented as 'hop length of rms feature (frame length is fixed)'

normalisation.source: S17 code, and paper equation (3) — PEAK normalisation, so the thresholds below are RELATIVE to the loudest frame of this signal and are therefore scale-free

max_segment_length_s.source: S17 paper, verbatim — 'matching Whisper's input duration'

min_cut_fallback.rule: when a segment would exceed the maximum and no prior silence is available, search only the SECOND HALF of the segment for the minimum VAD score and cut there; on ties take the LAST index.
min_cut_fallback.source: S17 code, the `else` branch of the max-duration switch-off

merge.rule: consecutive activity segments are merged while the merged span stays under max_segment_length_s

parameters_NOT_sourced.min_speech_duration_ms: read from VadOptions in their code; the value is faster-whisper's and was NOT verified this session
parameters_NOT_sourced.speech_pad_ms: same — comes from VadOptions and is unverified here
parameters_NOT_sourced.consequence: our implementation REQUIRES these two explicitly and has no default, because a silent default would be an unsourced threshold wearing a library's clothes.

their_asr.why_averaged: Whisper's decoding is stochastic; the paper averages error rates over 5 runs

our_asr.why: D-SSM-24 — everything must be Vertex and Google's own services. Whisper is not a Google service.
our_asr.consequence_stated_not_hidden: OUR NUMBERS WILL NOT BE COMPARABLE TO 20.35 %. That figure is Whisper-large-v2-on-Jam-ALT. Changing the ASR changes the instrument, so S17's WER is the METHOD's evidence, never our expected result. Any report that quotes 20.35 % as our target is wrong.

stage_3_asr.per_language_rule: the ASR is named per language in the artefact — S17/S01 both select a language-appropriate model (Paraformer for Mandarin, Whisper for English). For Turkish the choice is open and must be made with a control (Axis 7 gap).

per.why: PER is what the SVS literature reports for lyric intelligibility, and WER punishes Turkish for being agglutinative (S41 names Turkish in that argument).
per.softening_rule_verbatim: S05 (Transinger): 'detections that match the correct word or its homophones were not counted as errors. Moreover, if only a subset of the phonemes in a word is correctly detected, those correctly identified phonemes are also considered accurate.'
per.implemented_by: music_studio/per_gate.py — the existing lattice-based scorer already gives partial phoneme credit through alignment; the HOMOPHONE clause is the part A8 adds.

wer.why: comparability with the published frontier, which does not use PER at all.
wer.convention: case-insensitive WER as defined by alt-eval (S14/S16). For writing systems without spaces alt-eval treats each character as a word, making WER equivalent to CER.

stage_4_metrics.correction_carried_forward: D-SSM-18: 16.14 % PER is NOT a human floor — it is VAE-reconstructed ground truth measured on a MIX. No threshold in this gate comes from it.

human_floors_measured_by_others.why_recorded: they show the floor is PER-LANGUAGE by a factor of about 2.7, which is A9's justification — they are NOT our bar.

stage_5_the_vocable_exemption.rule: non-lexical vocables ('ooh', 'ah') and backing vocals must NOT count as lyric failure.
stage_5_the_vocable_exemption.measured_reason_verbatim: S17: 'over half of both are deleted in both datasets, revealing a shortcoming in Whisper... The high values observed even with vocal stems indicate that this issue cannot be resolved by improved source separation.'
stage_5_the_vocable_exemption.consequence: a song full of vocables would score as unintelligible when the singing is correct. This is A10's fourth negative control.

what_this_gate_cannot_do: It cannot say whether the singing is GOOD. It measures intelligibility only; the artistic verdict is Berk's (MANDATE CLAUSE 19).

It cannot produce a PASS/FAIL until A9's per-language bar is calibrated from >=5 real human sung recordings in that language. Until then every verdict is NOT_CALIBRATED and that is the honest state, not a placeholder.
